Nothing is placed while dry. order = the FOK limit the executor would send (YES-price convention, tick-rounded, contracts). execPriceC = volume-weighted effective price for the paper size; slippageC = cents worse than the paper price; wouldReject = live rules that would refuse it (min size, slippage cap 5c, thin book); wouldBlock = the daily risk gates. routing.unroutable = intents with no Polymarket US market (the live path skips those trades). roundTrips diff buy+sell (both fees) against the paper ledger; dryMinusPaper is how much paper overstates. Maker mode (orderMode): a BUY rests post-only at the best level on our side (good-till-date = the TTL) instead of crossing; dry fills it when the market trades through the level or a print lands there, and at the TTL takes the taker fill (fallback) or skips; takerRef on a maker fill is the FOK it would have sent at placement, so maker.savedVsTakerUsd and roundTrips.makerMinusTakerOnFilled are the maker edge on the trades that filled; maker.missed are entries that never filled. Exits stay taker. Live: only with paperTradeMode off and PMUS_KEY_ID/PMUS_SECRET_KEY set; consumes the live exec queue, FOK limit or close-position with synchronous execution, confirms fills to the auto-trader, reconciles ambiguous sends against the account position and halts itself if that fails. POST /autotrader/executor/halt is the kill switch.

scalp.read: The stale-quote scalp lane (src/scalp.js), two venues. Polymarket US (venue 'us', mode scalpMode): each minute the sampler sees global Polymarket's mid move 3c+ while the US quote has not followed and is still crossable after its taker fee, the lane takes the stale quote for up to $10 (never more than the shares shown, 50+ required) and closes on the US book 5 minutes later as a taker. Kalshi (venue 'kalshi', mode scalpKalshiMode, sports: NHL): the same minutes on Kalshi's own YES book for the leg, a stale ask bought as YES or a stale bid sold as YES (= buying NO), up to $10, closed on that book 5 minutes later; Kalshi sizes are not sampled, so dry assumes the quote holds for that size and live sends immediate-or-cancel orders that fill what is there or nothing. pnlC is cents a share after both of the venue's taker fees (Polymarket US 0.0695 x p(1-p), Kalshi 0.07 x p(1-p)), the number the paper lane's x5 mark reads for the US venue. Modes per venue: off / dry (decisions and fills at the sampled quotes, nothing sent) / live (real orders with that venue's key, only when it is on the worker: PMUS_* for Polymarket US, KALSHI_* for Kalshi). Risk: 3 open and 40 a day per venue, one stop at -$15 realized on the day across both, one scalp per game across venues, edge >= 1c; POST /xvenue/scalp/halt is the kill switch for both and the lane halts itself on an ambiguous send or an exit it cannot reconcile. byVenue splits the record. exitKind: x5 = closed at the hold on the venue's quote; late_last_quote / no_quote = no quote at the hold (dry), closed at the last quote seen or unpriced; x_live = the venue's fill (x_live_part = a partial Kalshi fill, the rest closed later); settling = the venue refused the close (market over), the position settles there and its P&L lands in the account balance, not here. The live flips are the owner's. probe (src/fill-probe.js, Nov 2 2026): every dry entry re-reads the venue's book a few seconds after the sampler's look (t0) and 10s later (t1); per venue, thereRate = the share of reads where the entry price was still quoted on our side, enoughRate = of those with sizes, the share with at least the scalp's size behind it, qtyMed = contracts left when it was there, goneAvgMoveC = how far the quote had moved against us when it was gone, avgS = seconds after the sample. This is the dry record's missing piece: whether the quote survives long enough for a live order to hit it. fresh (Nov 12 2026): until then every Polymarket US quote (sampler, probe) came off the gateway's edge cache, up to 30s old, next to a live global quote, and a dry scalp filled at the sampled quote for its whole size. Since fresh.since a dry US scalp is the live order itself matched on the venue's book read at the moment live would send it: the fill-or-kill fills only when the whole size is offered at or better than the tick-rounded limit, at the levels it takes, with the fee per level (today.drySent / dryFilled count them, as liveSent / liveFilled do for live), and the exit is close-position on the book read at the hold (x5; x5_part when the book is thin and the rest waits a minute; an empty side three minutes running is where live halts: no_quote, today.wouldHalt). fresh holds the US venue's record (all, byMode, bySport, probe) from then on and is the one to read for the live lane. Kalshi was always read live; its dry mode still fills at the sampled quote.

investigator.read: The AI investigator's settled record as bets: it backs the investigated direction when its probability is above the market's and the other side when below, a flat $100, held to settlement. core = the paper leaderboard's rule; wide = every disagreement of 5+ points. roi.recorded is at the price recorded when it looked (Gamma's displayed probability, not an offer); c1/c2/c3 pay 1/2/3 cents more per contract plus a 0.07 x p(1-p) exchange fee, which is the range a real fill on Kalshi or Polymarket US would land in. hitPct against breakEvenPct (the average price paid) is the edge in points. events = distinct events behind the bets (buckets of one event share a cluster); tEvents / tEventsC2 = mean return over its standard error with one event's bets summed first, at the recorded price and under c2: about 2 or more is evidence, under 1 is noise. byMinEdge runs the rule at each disagreement size: a real edge grows with it. concentration shows how much is a few long shots. calibration compares Brier scores (lower is better) on every scored investigation by kind. openDrift = on the open investigations, cents the market has moved toward the agent's view since it looked. Markets are global Polymarket's; a US account would trade the same question on Kalshi where it lists one.

test.rule: Bet $25 when the AI investigator's probability for a side is 20+ points above the price actually paid for it in the order book, the question settles within 72 hours, its confidence is not LOW and the market is not weather. Held to settlement. Paper only.
test.read: The pattern from the settled record, tested forward with the rule fixed in advance (version 1). Each bet is the order a live bot would send the moment the research finishes: buy up to $25 from the real asks of the side it backs, cheapest first, never above its probability minus 20 points; what is offered there is the fill (partial when the book is thin), nothing offered there is no bet (whyNot). settled: hitPct against breakEvenPct (the average price paid), and the result before fees, with Polymarket's own fee schedule and with Kalshi's 0.07 x p(1-p) (the US venue's cost: the number to read). events = distinct events behind the bets; tEvents = mean return over its standard error with one event's bets summed first (about 2 or more is evidence, under 1 is noise). fill.avgPaidOverShownC = cents paid over the price shown when the research started. atEdge = the rule at other disagreement sizes, the whole stake at the real offer. The book is global Polymarket's; Kalshi's price for the same question can differ.
